name: Composite bonding
summary: Tooth-coloured resin shaped and light-cured onto teeth to mask chips, gaps and stains; an established dental technique, with durability varying by material and technique.
lead: Composite bonding, also called dental bonding, is the attachment of a tooth-coloured resin to natural enamel and dentin; the dentist applies the resin and cures it with visible blue light so it bonds to the tooth and improves its appearance . Direct composite bonding is used to repair cracks or gaps .

name: Dental cleaning / scale and polish
summary: Hygienist removal of tartar and surface stain; a routine dental service whose benefit for healthy adults is judged uncertain by a Cochrane review.
lead: Dental cleaning, often called scale and polish, is professional removal of plaque, calculus (tartar) and surface stain from the teeth by a dental hygienist or dentist. A regular cleaning includes scaling and polishing but not root planing, which is part of deeper gum treatment .

name: Air polishing (Airflow)
summary: A dentist's powder-jet cleaning that lifts surface stain; it changes surface colour, not the tooth's intrinsic shade.
lead: Air polishing, often called by the brand-derived name Airflow, is a dental procedure in which a handpiece sprays a pressurised mix of water, air and fine powder onto the teeth to remove extrinsic stains and soft deposits such as plaque biofilm. It is performed by dentists and hygienists, usually during a cleaning visit, and is discussed in appearance circles as a way to lift coffee, tea, wine and tobacco staining without scraping.

name: Violet toothpaste (V34 colour corrector)
summary: A purple-tinted toothpaste that makes yellow teeth look whiter through colour optics; no studies back it yet.
lead: Violet toothpaste, with V34 as a widely discussed example, is a cosmetic product that deposits a thin violet pigment on the teeth. Proponents say that because violet lies opposite yellow on the colour wheel, it makes yellowish teeth look whiter for a short time, without any peroxide.

name: Purple toothpaste / colour corrector serum
summary: A purple paste or serum that visually offsets yellow teeth; a trend product with no published studies.
lead: Purple toothpastes and colour corrector serums are cosmetic dental products, popular in short-video trends, that apply a purple pigment to the teeth to give an instant whiter look. They are marketed as a peroxide-free alternative to bleaching.

name: Whitening pens
summary: Peroxide gel pens for quick touch-ups; studied only in labs so far.
lead: Whitening pens are over-the-counter applicator pens holding a peroxide-based gel that users paint onto the front of the teeth, mainly for touch-ups between longer bleaching courses. Colgate Optic White, Equate and Zimba-branded pens have been among those tested in laboratory work.

name: Whitening mouthwash
summary: Daily peroxide or non-peroxide rinses sold to whiten; research so far is lab-based.
lead: Whitening mouthwashes are rinses, some containing hydrogen peroxide and others non-peroxide agents, sold to lighten teeth or reduce staining with daily use. Listerine Whitening is one product examined in laboratory research.

name: Whitening powder (charcoal)
summary: Brush-on activated charcoal powder for surface stain; only lab research exists.
lead: Charcoal whitening powders are products of activated charcoal that users brush onto teeth with the aim of removing surface stain. They are one of several consumer whitening formats alongside strips, pens, rinses and toothpastes.

name: Activated charcoal toothpaste
summary: Black 'natural' whitening toothpaste that studies so far show is more abrasive than it is effective, with no ADA Seal.
lead: Activated charcoal toothpaste is a category of over-the-counter dentifrice, sold as pastes and powders, that includes finely powdered activated charcoal as its headline ingredient and is marketed for removing extrinsic (surface) stains and whitening teeth . Activated charcoal is carbon processed to be highly porous; the claimed actions are adsorption of stain particles and mild abrasion .
claims: Charcoal adsorbs stains and whitens teeth quickly
Charcoal toothpaste is a safe natural alternative to bleaching

name: Baking soda brushing
summary: Brushing with sodium bicarbonate, a mild abrasive for surface stains that is also an established toothpaste ingredient.
lead: Baking soda brushing is the practice of cleaning teeth with sodium bicarbonate, either through commercial toothpastes that contain it or as a home-made paste, usually to remove surface stain. Sodium bicarbonate is also used as an ingredient in some mouthwashes, where it is described as having anticaries and abrasive properties .

name: Hydrogen peroxide rinse DIY
summary: Swishing diluted household hydrogen peroxide for whiter teeth, with irritation concerns and thin direct evidence.
lead: A hydrogen peroxide rinse is a do-it-yourself practice in which diluted household hydrogen peroxide, commonly the 3 percent pharmacy solution, is swished in the mouth, usually for whitening or breath and gum goals. It draws on the fact that hydrogen peroxide, directly or as carbamide peroxide, is the most common active ingredient in tooth whitening .

name: Baking soda and peroxide paste
summary: A home-made brushing paste of baking soda and hydrogen peroxide; each part has some evidence, the mix itself has little.
lead: Baking soda and peroxide paste is a home-made tooth-cleaning mixture of sodium bicarbonate and hydrogen peroxide. Wikipedia notes that hydrogen peroxide can be mixed with baking soda and salt to make a homemade toothpaste .

name: Oil pulling
summary: Swishing coconut or sesame oil, an Ayurvedic practice with small trials on gum health and no solid evidence for whitening.
lead: Oil pulling is a traditional practice from Ayurvedic medicine in which edible oil, commonly sesame, coconut or sunflower, is swished in the mouth and then spat out, similar to using a mouthwash . Ayurvedic texts refer to it as kavala or gandusha, and it is promoted for oral hygiene, bad breath, gum health and, in modern wellness circles, tooth whitening .
claims: Oil pulling improves breath and removes bacteria

name: Strawberry and baking soda hack
summary: Mashed-strawberry and baking soda paste promoted as a natural whitener; no studies found, and dental sources warn about dietary acid.
lead: The strawberry and baking soda hack is a do-it-yourself teeth-whitening remedy in which mashed strawberries are mixed with baking soda and applied to the teeth. It is promoted as a natural alternative to peroxide-based whitening.
claims: Strawberry malic acid plus baking soda whitens teeth

name: Banana peel teeth whitening
summary: Rubbing banana peel on teeth is a folk whitening trick; no clinical studies of it were found.
lead: Banana peel teeth whitening is a home practice in which the inside of a banana peel is rubbed on the teeth, usually for a few minutes a day, in the hope of making them look whiter. It is shared as a low-cost, natural alternative to peroxide whitening and is discussed in appearance and oral-care circles as a folk remedy.

name: Orange peel teeth whitening
summary: Rubbing orange peel on teeth is a folk whitening trick; no trials exist and citrus acid is a known erosion factor.
lead: Orange peel teeth whitening is a home practice of rubbing the inner side of an orange or other citrus peel on the teeth to make them look whiter. It is shared online as a natural, inexpensive alternative to commercial whitening products.

name: Apple cider vinegar whitening
summary: ACV rinses are a popular natural whitening trick; no trials exist, and acid erosion of enamel is the documented concern.
lead: Apple cider vinegar (ACV) whitening is a home practice of swishing diluted or undiluted apple cider vinegar around the mouth, or applying it to the teeth, in the hope of removing stains. It is circulated as a natural whitening rinse.

name: Lemon juice whitening
summary: Lemon juice on teeth is a popular natural whitening idea; no trials were found and citric acid is a known erosion factor.
lead: Lemon juice whitening is a home practice of applying lemon juice, alone or mixed with baking soda, to the teeth to remove stains. It is shared as a natural bleaching method.

name: Turmeric toothpaste
summary: Turmeric toothpaste is a natural-whitening idea; no trials were found, and turmeric is itself a staining pigment.
lead: Turmeric toothpaste is a homemade paste, or a commercial toothpaste, containing turmeric powder and is marketed or shared as a natural whitening product. The idea is counterintuitive, since turmeric is a strong yellow pigment.

name: Neem twig / miswak
summary: Traditional chewing sticks with a long history; small observational studies on gum health, no whitening trials.
lead: Chewing sticks are twigs whose frayed ends are used as natural toothbrushes. The best known is miswak, from the Salvadora persica tree, traditionally used in the Middle East; neem (Azadirachta indica) twigs are commonly used the same way in southern India and the Middle East .

name: Coconut oil toothpaste
summary: Coconut-oil-and-baking-soda tooth paste sold as a gentle natural whitener; no trial shows it whitens.
lead: Coconut oil toothpaste is a category of homemade or commercially sold "natural" tooth cleaner in which coconut oil is a principal ingredient, usually mixed with baking soda or similar powders. It is promoted in online looksmaxxing and wellness circles as a gentler, additive-free way to clean and whiten teeth.

name: Fluoride-free natural toothpaste
summary: Herbal or DIY pastes without fluoride, sold as clean alternatives; plaque data are low quality and fluoride-free pastes lack caries data.
lead: Fluoride-free natural toothpaste refers to herbal, mineral or homemade dentifrices that omit fluoride and often other conventional additives. They are marketed to people who want to avoid artificial ingredients, and DIY recipes are a recurring trend in appearance and wellness communities.

name: Tooth filing / enamel shaving DIY
summary: Home filing or sanding of teeth for shape or shade; dentists describe enamel loss as permanent and no studies exist.
lead: Tooth filing or enamel shaving at home is the practice of using a file, sanding tool or similar abrasive to alter the shape, length or shade of one's own teeth without a dentist. Participants in appearance forums discuss it as a way to even out edges or lighten teeth.

name: Dental sandpaper strips
summary: Online abrasive strips sold for scrubbing off tooth stains; no studies and no standard abrasivity data.
lead: Dental sandpaper strips are abrasive strips sold online, mainly through marketplaces, that are marketed for scraping stains off teeth. They are distinct from peroxide whitening strips, which use a chemical bleaching agent.

name: Straw drinking for coffee
summary: Sipping coffee through a straw to keep it off the front teeth; plausible to fans, but untested.
lead: Straw drinking for coffee is the habit of sipping coffee or other dark drinks through a straw so that less liquid touches the front teeth, in order to reduce visible staining. It is discussed in tooth-whitening and appearance communities as a low-effort preventive habit.

name: Water rinse after coffee
summary: Swishing water after coffee to cut stain build-up; harmless habit with no stain data.
lead: Rinsing the mouth with plain water after drinking coffee is a habit discussed in tooth-whitening and appearance communities as a way to reduce stain build-up.

name: Quit smoking for teeth
summary: Stopping tobacco stops new tar staining and gum harm, but old stains still need a cleaning.
lead: Quitting smoking for teeth refers to stopping tobacco use as a way of preventing or reducing the yellow-brown-black staining and other oral changes associated with smoking. Tar from smoke and smokeless tobacco forms a stain on the tooth surface, typically near the gumline, which dental references classify as extrinsic (surface) discolouration.

name: Prefab veneers (Snap-On Smile)
summary: Removable clip-on tooth covers sold as an instant smile; no research on them was found.
lead: Prefab or snap-on veneers are removable cosmetic covers marketed to sit over the front teeth to change their apparent colour, shape or spacing without dentistry. They differ from bonded veneers, which are made of composite or porcelain and attached to the tooth, and which are discussed in dental references as thin coverings for discolouration, enamel defects, fractures and shape changes.

name: Lumineers / no-prep veneers
summary: Very thin porcelain veneers with little or no grinding; the category is poorly sourced in general references.
lead: No-prep veneers are ultra-thin porcelain veneers that require little or no reduction of natural tooth structure; Lumineers is a commercial brand commonly associated with the category. A general encyclopedia article on veneers describes non-prep veneers in this way but flags the claim as needing a better source.

name: Tetracycline stain bleaching
summary: Weeks of overnight tray bleaching aimed at deep tetracycline stains, which resist normal whitening.
lead: Tetracycline stain bleaching is the use of extended peroxide bleaching, often worn overnight over weeks or months, to lighten the intrinsic yellow-grey-brown discolouration caused by tetracycline antibiotics taken during tooth development.
